entries.proposition: Design: multicentre prospective observational study of 36 patients aged 2 to 18 with six visits over 24 months, sized for exploratory and descriptive results.
entries.snippet: The number of patients was sufficiently sized to provide exploratory and descriptive results.

entries.proposition: Vineland and Bayley raw scores were converted to growth scale values so that change over time can be measured on an equal-interval scale.
entries.snippet: Raw scores from the Vineland-3 were converted to growth scale values (GSVs), which are reflective of the patient's absolute level of performance on an equal interval scale and are useful for measuring change over time.

entries.proposition: The Bayley scale was used outside its intended age range, chosen by chronological age and baseline test performance.
entries.snippet: Although the BSID-III is intended for use in patients up to the age of 42 months, in BUTTERFLY it was administered based on the patient's chronological age and baseline test performance

entries.proposition: Disease progression was modelled with repeated-measures mixed models using all patients with baseline and one later assessment, assuming data missing at random.
entries.snippet: Patients were included in disease progression models if they completed a baseline assessment and at least 1 postbaseline assessment.

entries.proposition: Of 36 enrolled, 21 completed; 15 withdrew, 8 of them to a sponsor phase 1/2a trial of a gene-directed therapy.
entries.snippet: Overall, 21 patients completed the study, while 15 patients withdrew before end of study (noncompleters) (Figure 1).

entries.proposition: Eight participants left the natural history study to join the sponsor interventional trial.
entries.snippet: including 8 patients who transferred to the MONARCH phase 1/2a study (NCT04442295).

entries.proposition: Only two of six modelled Vineland subdomains changed significantly over 24 months: receptive communication and coping skills.
entries.snippet: Disease progression modeling performed using individual subdomain GSVs indicated a statistically significant improvement in Receptive Communication (+7.24; 95% CI 1.30–13.19; p = 0.02) and Coping Skills (+4.61; 95% CI 1.14–8.08; p = 0.01) through Month 24

entries.proposition: The receptive communication gain was about three months of age-equivalent over 24 months.
entries.snippet: The estimated gain in age-equivalence over 24 months was 3 months for Receptive Communication.

entries.proposition: Baseline score was a positive predictor of change; baseline seizure frequency was not a significant covariate for Vineland subdomains.
entries.snippet: Baseline seizure frequency was not a significant covariate across any of the analyzed Vineland-3 subdomains.

entries.proposition: The Bayley subtests showed no significant change and very wide intervals with 10 to 13 patients.
entries.snippet: Modeling indicated lack of statistically significant changes across all BSID-III subtests through Month 24

entries.proposition: Convulsive seizure frequency did not change significantly over 24 months despite optimisation of standard care.
entries.snippet: Disease progression modeling indicated no significant change in convulsive seizure frequency through Month 24 in BUTTERFLY patients (+10.61; 95% CI −32.97 to 54.19; p = 0.63)

entries.proposition: The caregiver global impression showed a change at p 0.04 while the clinician impression did not (p 0.30); the baseline seizure frequency predicted less improvement.
entries.snippet: Modeling for the CaGI-C, but not CGI-C, indicated a statistically significant change (p = 0.04 for CaGI-C; p = 0.30 for CGI-C) through Month 24.

entries.proposition: The authors state a general plateau at about 2 years of developmental age despite standard care.
entries.snippet: showed a general plateau at a developmental age of approximately 2 years despite the use of recommended SOC ASMs

entries.proposition: About two thirds were at or below floor on one Vineland subdomain by age-equivalent at baseline.
entries.snippet: baseline data indicated that two-thirds of the patients scored at or below floor in the Coping Skills subdomain based on age-equivalent values.

entries.proposition: Limitations include substantial attrition, no enrolment guidelines (possible selection bias), recall bias, assessments outside validated age ranges and no neurotypical control group.
entries.snippet: The lack of a dedicated control group of neurotypical peers makes contextualizing the observed trajectories more challenging.

entries.proposition: The authors state future interventional studies must evaluate whether patients can regain their developmental trajectory.
entries.snippet: Future interventional studies will be crucial in evaluating the ability of patients across the age range to regain their developmental trajectory with targeted interventions.

entries.proposition: Fig 2: individual patient GSV lines scatter by about 10 to 30 points between visits around flat or slowly rising mean progressions, with the dashed population-norm line constructed from the manual starting at the cohort mean age equivalent.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 2 six panels (receptive and expressive communication, gross and fine motor, coping and personal skills): thin grey lines for individual patients with visit-to-visit wiggles of several to a few tens of GSV points, a solid mean line nearly flat or slowly rising (gross motor falling) and a blue dashed population-norm line rising more steeply from the cohort baseline age-equivalent (19, 22, 23, 28, 24 and 28 months).

entries.proposition: Fig 1: 40 consented, 4 not enrolled, 36 enrolled with 12 per age group; 21 completed (8, 8 and 5 by age group) and 15 withdrew, 14 for other reasons including 8 transfers.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 1 flow chart: consented 40; screen failures 2; early discontinuation 2; enrolled 36 (12 per age group); completed 21 (58.3 percent: 8 aged 2-7, 8 aged 8-12, 5 aged 13-18); withdrawn 15 (41.7 percent): intercurrent illness 1, other 14 including 8 transferred to MONARCH.

entries.proposition: Fig 3: Bayley growth score equivalents trace a flat mean line against a rising population-norm line, with very few individual points per panel.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 3 five panels (cognitive, receptive and expressive communication, gross and fine motor): solid mean line flat or declining (receptive and fine motor falling) with sparse individual points and wide scatter; blue dashed population line rising from the cohort baseline age-equivalent (16 to 20 months).
